## alertmanager

### config/

- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Configure Alertmanager for Tailscale Ingress mode. Alertmanager has no built-in authentication — auth is handled at the network level by Tailscale. This playbook sets --web.external-url so Alertmanager generates correct links when accessed via the tailnet, waits for the rollout, and verifies the /-/healthy endpoint.
- **`05-wire-awx.yml`** — Configure Alertmanager to send critical alerts to AWX for auto-remediation. Patches the alertmanager-config ConfigMap to add an awx-webhook receiver that POSTs to AWX job template launch endpoint with Bearer auth, and adds a route for severity=critical alerts. Restarts Alertmanager to pick up the new configuration.
- **`06-enable-metrics.yml`** — Add Prometheus scrape annotations to the Alertmanager workload. Alertmanager natively exposes metrics on port 9093 at /metrics. This playbook discovers whether Alertmanager runs as a statefulset or deployment, then adds pod-level annotations so Prometheus auto-discovers and scrapes the metrics endpoint via its kubernetes-pods scrape config.

### install/

- **`01-apply-kustomize.yml`** — Deploy Alertmanager via Kustomize
  - Templates: `configmap.yaml.j2`, `statefulset.yaml.j2`, `service.yaml.j2`
- **`02-verify.yml`** — Verify Alertmanager deployment is healthy

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

## argocd

### config/

- **`01-get-admin-password.yml`** — Retrieve ArgoCD admin password and optionally store in BWS
- **`02-configure-repositories.yml`** — Configure ArgoCD Git repositories with credentials from BWS
- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Enable anonymous read-only access for ArgoCD in Tailscale mode. Patches argocd-cm ConfigMap to enable anonymous users and argocd-rbac-cm to grant read-only role. Tailscale provides the authentication layer.
- **`05-wire-awx.yml`** — Configure ArgoCD Notifications to send webhook events to AWX on successful app syncs. Patches the argocd-notifications-cm ConfigMap to add a webhook service, notification template, and trigger for sync-succeeded events. The notifications controller auto-reloads ConfigMap changes.
- **`06-enable-metrics.yml`** — Add Prometheus scrape annotations to ArgoCD application-controller and argocd-server deployments. Both already expose metrics natively (controller on port 8082, server on port 8083). This playbook adds pod-level annotations so Prometheus auto-discovers and scrapes both endpoints via its kubernetes-pods scrape config.

### install/

- **`01-apply-kustomize.yml`** — Deploy ArgoCD via Kustomize
- **`02-verify.yml`** — Verify ArgoCD deployment is healthy

### operations/

- **`application-create.yml`** — Create an ArgoCD application with source, destination, and sync policy. Supports Git and Helm sources, Kustomize overlays, and automated sync. This operation is idempotent - existing applications can be updated.
- **`cluster-create.yml`** — Register a Kubernetes cluster with ArgoCD. Supports bearer token auth, TLS client certificates, AWS EKS auth, and exec-based authentication. The in-cluster (https://kubernetes.default.svc) is registered by default.
- **`project-create.yml`** — Create an ArgoCD project with source/destination restrictions and RBAC. This operation is idempotent - if a project with the same name exists, it can be updated or skipped based on the upsert parameter.
- **`repository-create.yml`** — Register a Git or Helm repository with ArgoCD. Supports SSH keys, HTTP(S) authentication, GitHub App authentication, and TLS client certs. This operation is idempotent - existing repositories can be updated.

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-argocd-config.yml`** — Verify that ArgoCD is properly configured and healthy. Checks that the API server is accessible, projects exist with expected settings, repositories are connected and synced, clusters are registered and reachable, applications are synced and healthy, and ApplicationSets are generating expected apps. Provides a comprehensive health report.

## authentik

### config/

- **`00-create-admin-user.yml`** — Create an authentik admin (superuser) using console credentials from BWS. Reads username and password from shared BWS secrets. Idempotent — skips creation if user already exists, updates password if user exists.
- **`01-create-oauth-apps.yml`** — Auto-generate OAuth applications in Authentik for all apps with sso.enabled: true from registry metadata. Supports both Cloudflare Tunnel and Tailscale MagicDNS ingress modes.
- **`02-wire-forwardauth.yml`** — Create Authentik ForwardAuth Middleware CRD. ForwardAuth middleware references are baked into IngressRoutes at creation time by 01-create-ingressroutes.yml. This playbook only creates the Middleware CRD itself and writes state to BWS.
- **`03-create-proxy-providers.yml`** — Create authentik proxy providers (forward_single mode) and applications for all Cloudflare-mode SSO-enabled apps. Uses embedded outpost (auto-discovers providers). ForwardAuth address stays cluster-internal.
- **`04-enable-metrics.yml`** — Add Prometheus scrape annotations to the authentik-server deployment. Authentik natively exposes metrics on port 9300 at /metrics. This playbook discovers the correct deployment name via the app.kubernetes.io/name=authentik label, then adds pod-level annotations so Prometheus auto-discovers and scrapes the metrics endpoint via its kubernetes-pods scrape config.
- **`create_oauth_app.yml`** — Playbook: create_oauth_app.yml

### install/

- **`01-deploy.yml`** — Deploy Authentik identity provider via J2 templates. Includes bundled PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7. Secrets from K8s Secret (ESO will sync real values). Accessible via NodePort 30900.
  - Templates: `secrets.yaml.j2`, `postgres.yaml.j2`, `redis.yaml.j2`, `server.yaml.j2`, `worker.yaml.j2`, `blueprints-configmap.yaml.j2`, `forwardauth-middleware.yaml.j2`, `ingressroute.yaml.j2`
- **`02-verify.yml`** — Verify Authentik deployment is healthy

### operations/

- **`core-applications-create.yml`** — Create an application in Authentik and link it to an OAuth2 provider. This operation is idempotent - if an application with the same slug exists, it will be skipped. The application appears in the user portal and controls access to the linked provider.
- **`outposts-instances-create.yml`** — Create an outpost in Authentik to deploy the proxy/LDAP/RADIUS frontend. Outposts handle the actual authentication flow for applications. This operation is idempotent - if an outpost with the same name exists, it will be updated with new provider list if different.
- **`providers-oauth2-create.yml`** — Create an OAuth2 provider in Authentik. This operation is idempotent - if a provider with the same name exists, it will be skipped. Returns the provider ID for use in application creation.

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-sso-protection.yml`** — Verify that a web application is protected by Authentik SSO. Checks OAuth provider exists, application exists, ForwardAuth middleware is configured, and unauthenticated requests redirect to Authentik for authentication.

## awx

### config/

- **`01-configure-repo-sync.yml`** — Configure AWX repository sync and create initial inventory and job templates
- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Configure AWX Django settings for Tailscale Ingress mode. Sets CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, REMOTE_HOST_HEADERS, and ALLOWED_HOSTS via the AWX REST API so that requests proxied through the Tailscale operator are not blocked by Django CSRF protection. Tailscale provides the authentication layer.
- **`04-configure-traefik-ingress.yml`** — Deploy AWX with Traefik IngressRoute and Authentik OAuth2 SSO
- **`05-wire-vault.yml`** — Wire AWX to HashiCorp Vault as a credential backend. Creates a "HashiCorp Vault Secret Lookup" credential in AWX pointing at Vault's KV v2 engine via internal K8s DNS. This credential can then be linked to Machine credentials as an input_source, allowing AWX job templates to pull secrets from Vault at runtime.

### install/

- **`01-deploy-operator.yml`** — Deploy AWX operator and instance for in-cluster Ansible automation

### operations/

- **`credential-create.yml`** — Create an AWX credential for authentication (SSH, SCM, cloud, etc.). This operation is idempotent - if a credential with the same name exists in the organization, it will be skipped. Supports all credential types.
- **`inventory-create.yml`** — Create an AWX inventory for host management. This operation is idempotent - if an inventory with the same name exists, it will be skipped. Supports standard, smart, and constructed inventory types.
- **`job-template-create.yml`** — Create an AWX job template for playbook execution. This operation is idempotent - if a job template with the same name exists, it will be skipped. Supports all job template options including credentials, survey, and launch settings.
- **`job-template-launch.yml`** — Launch a job from an AWX job template with optional runtime overrides. Can optionally wait for job completion and return status. Supports extra vars, limit, tags, and other launch-time parameters.
- **`project-create.yml`** — Create an AWX project for SCM-based playbook management. This operation is idempotent - if a project with the same name exists, it will be skipped. Supports all project parameters including SCM type, URL, branch, and credentials.
- **`project-sync.yml`** — Trigger an SCM update for an AWX project to pull latest changes from the repository. Waits for the sync job to complete and reports status.

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-awx-config.yml`** — Verify that AWX is properly configured. Checks that the API is accessible, projects exist and are synced, inventories have expected hosts, credentials are valid, job templates are properly configured, and optionally verifies recent job runs completed successfully. Provides a comprehensive health check.

## cert-manager

### config/

- **`01-cloudflare-origin-cert.yml`** — Configure cert-manager with Cloudflare Origin CA for edge certificates
- **`05-wire-vault-pki.yml`** — Create a cert-manager ClusterIssuer backed by Vault PKI for internal cluster TLS certificates. Enables the Vault PKI secrets engine, generates an internal root CA, configures a role for cluster.local domains, creates a Vault policy and K8s auth role for cert-manager, and applies the ClusterIssuer CRD. Uses K8s service account auth (no API keys needed).
- **`06-enable-metrics.yml`** — Add Prometheus scrape annotations to the cert-manager controller deployment. cert-manager natively exposes metrics on port 9402 at /metrics. This playbook adds pod-level annotations so Prometheus auto-discovers and scrapes the metrics endpoint via its kubernetes-pods scrape config.

## cloudflare

### config/

- **`01-create-origin-certs.yml`** — Create Cloudflare origin certificates for all installed Cloudflare-mode apps. Uses BWS cache for credential resolution, REGISTRY_PATH for app discovery, per-app ingress mode overrides, and stores certs in each app's own namespace.
- **`02-configure-tunnel-and-dns.yml`** — Configure Cloudflare Tunnel ingress rules and create DNS CNAME records dynamically from registry.json + installed apps. Routes all traffic through Traefik. Includes auth.{domain} for authentik.

### install/

- **`01-deploy-tunnel.yml`** — Create Cloudflare Tunnel via API (or reuse existing), deploy cloudflared K8s Deployment with tunnel token, and write tunnel state to BWS.
  - Templates: `cloudflared-deployment.yaml.j2`

### operations/

- **`certificates-create.yml`** — Create a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate for a specific hostname. Generates a CSR, requests the certificate via Cloudflare API, stores the result in a Kubernetes TLS secret, and writes certificate metadata to BWS._state.

### uninstall/

- **`01-cleanup-tunnel-and-dns.yml`** — Clean up all Cloudflare resources for a VM: delete DNS CNAME records, delete the Cloudflare Tunnel, and clear BWS state. Used during VM destroy.
- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-origin-cert.yml`** — Verify that a Cloudflare origin certificate exists and is properly stored in Kubernetes. Checks certificate exists in Cloudflare, TLS secret exists in K8s with valid keys, certificate is not expired, and certificate matches the expected hostname.

## elastic

### config/

- **`01-configure-credentials.yml`** — Configure Elasticsearch credentials and optionally store in BWS
- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Disable xpack security for Elasticsearch in Tailscale mode. ## external-secrets

### config/

- **`04-wire-vault.yml`** — Wire External Secrets Operator to HashiCorp Vault by creating a ClusterSecretStore backed by Vault's KV v2 engine using token auth. Creates a K8s Secret holding the Vault token, then applies the ClusterSecretStore CRD pointing at Vault's internal DNS address. Any namespace can then create ExternalSecret resources referencing this store to pull secrets from Vault.
- **`05-enable-metrics.yml`** — Add Prometheus scrape annotations to the external-secrets controller deployment. External Secrets Operator natively exposes metrics on port 8080 at /metrics. This playbook adds pod-level annotations so Prometheus auto-discovers and scrapes the metrics endpoint via its kubernetes-pods scrape config.

### install/

- **`01-deploy-kubectl.yml`** — Deploy External Secrets Operator via Helm (Vault integration is Phase 4)
- **`02-verify.yml`** — Verify External Secrets Operator deployment is healthy

### operations/

- **`clustersecretstore-create.yml`** — Create a cluster-scoped ClusterSecretStore for External Secrets Operator. ClusterSecretStores can be referenced from any namespace in the cluster. Supports Vault (with Kubernetes auth, token auth, AppRole) and BWS providers. This operation is idempotent - existing stores are updated in place.
- **`externalsecret-create.yml`** — Create an ExternalSecret to sync secrets from an external provider (Vault, BWS, etc.) into a Kubernetes Secret. Supports individual key mapping, dataFrom for bulk sync, and templating for custom Secret formats. This operation is idempotent.
- **`secretstore-create.yml`** — Create a namespace-scoped SecretStore for External Secrets Operator. Supports Vault (with Kubernetes auth, token auth, AppRole) and BWS providers. This operation is idempotent - existing SecretStores are updated in place.

### render/

- **`00-render-manifests.yml`** — Render External Secrets Operator manifests from J2 templates using BWS inventory variables
  - Templates: `service.yaml.j2`

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-eso-config.yml`** — Verify External Secrets Operator configuration is complete and functioning: - SecretStore/ClusterSecretStore is ready and can connect to backend - ExternalSecret is syncing successfully - Target Kubernetes Secrets are created with expected keys - Optional: Test secret value retrieval (without exposing values)

## grafana

### config/

- **`01-configure-datasources.yml`** — Configure Grafana datasources by reading BWS._state for Loki and Prometheus URLs. Wires Grafana to available datasources via API (no kubectl). Updates BWS._state with wiring status.
- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Enable anonymous access for Grafana in Tailscale mode. Patches the Grafana deployment with GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true so users on the tailnet can access dashboards without logging in. Tailscale provides the authentication layer.
- **`04-configure-datasources.yml`** — Configure Grafana datasources via API
- **`05-wire-prometheus.yml`** — Add Prometheus as the default datasource in Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses Grafana basic auth (admin user) and internal K8s DNS for the Prometheus URL. Idempotent: 409 means datasource already exists.
- **`06-wire-loki.yml`** — Add Loki as a datasource in Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses Grafana basic auth (admin user) and internal K8s DNS for the Loki URL. Idempotent: checks for existing datasource before creating.
- **`07-wire-alertmanager.yml`** — Add Alertmanager as a datasource in Grafana via the HTTP API. Configures the Prometheus implementation type so Grafana can query Alertmanager's API for alert status and silences. Idempotent: checks for existing datasource before creating.
- **`08-wire-elastic.yml`** — Add Elasticsearch as a datasource in Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses internal K8s DNS for the Elasticsearch URL. Configures the logs-* index pattern with @timestamp as the time field. Idempotent: checks for existing datasource before creating.
- **`09-wire-alertmanager-unified.yml`** — Configure Grafana unified alerting to send alerts to Alertmanager. This is the push direction (Grafana -> Alertmanager). The existing 07-wire-alertmanager.yml adds Alertmanager as a datasource (pull). This playbook enables unified alerting via environment variables on the Grafana deployment, disables legacy alerting, and configures the external Alertmanager URL. Idempotent: checks current env vars before patching.
- **`10-enable-metrics.yml`** — Enable Prometheus metrics scraping for Grafana. Sets the GF_METRICS_ENABLED=true environment variable to activate the built-in /metrics endpoint on port 3000, then adds pod-level Prometheus scrape annotations so Prometheus auto-discovers and scrapes the metrics endpoint via its kubernetes-pods scrape config.
- **`11-dashboard-traefik.yml`** — Import Traefik v3 Overview dashboard (Grafana.com #17346) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`12-dashboard-longhorn.yml`** — Import Longhorn v1 dashboard (Grafana.com #16888) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`13-dashboard-certmanager.yml`** — Import cert-manager dashboard (Grafana.com #20842) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`14-dashboard-vault.yml`** — Import Vault Overview dashboard (Grafana.com #12904) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`15-dashboard-argocd.yml`** — Import ArgoCD Overview dashboard (Grafana.com #14584) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`16-dashboard-authentik.yml`** — Import Authentik dashboard (Grafana.com #14837) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`17-dashboard-teleport.yml`** — Import Teleport dashboard (Grafana.com #15399) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`18-dashboard-sonarr.yml`** — Import Sonarr v3 dashboard (Grafana.com #12530) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`19-dashboard-radarr.yml`** — Import Radarr v3 dashboard (Grafana.com #12896) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`20-dashboard-qbittorrent.yml`** — Import qBittorrent Dashboard (Grafana.com #15116) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`21-dashboard-sabnzbd.yml`** — Import SABnzbd dashboard (Grafana.com #9567) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`22-dashboard-plex.yml`** — Import Plex Template dashboard (Grafana.com #17891) into Grafana via the HTTP API. Uses basic auth and the /api/dashboards/import endpoint. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.
- **`23-dashboard-jellyfin.yml`** — Import Jellyfin Overview dashboard into Grafana via the HTTP API. No Grafana.com dashboard exists for Jellyfin; uses a minimal inline dashboard JSON with placeholder panels. Replace with a community dashboard JSON (e.g. rebelcore/jellyfin_grafana) when available. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.

No Grafana.com dashboard exists for Prowlarr; uses a minimal inline dashboard JSON with placeholder panels. Replace with the Exportarr community dashboard JSON when available. Idempotent: uses overwrite=true so re-runs update the existing dashboard.

- **`26-datasource-langfuse.yml`** — Install the Grafana Infinity datasource plugin and add Langfuse as a datasource for querying Langfuse metrics via its HTTP API. Requires a Grafana pod restart to load the plugin. Uses internal K8s DNS for Langfuse connectivity.

### install/

- **`01-deploy.yml`** — Deploy Grafana visualization and dashboards to K3s cluster. Provides unified observability UI for metrics and logs. Accessible via Tailscale on NodePort 30300.
  - Templates: `configmap.yaml.j2`, `secrets.yaml.j2`, `statefulset.yaml.j2`, `service.yaml.j2`
- **`02-verify.yml`** — Verify Grafana deployment is healthy

### operations/

- **`alertrule-create.yml`** — Create an alert rule in Grafana using the Alerting Provisioning API. This operation is idempotent - if an alert rule with the same title in the same folder/group exists, it will be skipped. Supports all alert rule types including Prometheus-style queries.
- **`dashboard-import.yml`** — Import a dashboard into Grafana. This operation is idempotent - if overwrite is false and dashboard exists, it will be skipped. Supports importing from JSON file, inline JSON, or Grafana.com ID.
- **`datasource-create.yml`** — Create a datasource in Grafana. This operation is idempotent - if a datasource with the same name exists, it will be skipped. Supports all datasource types (prometheus, loki, elasticsearch, etc.).
- **`folder-create.yml`** — Create a folder in Grafana for organizing dashboards. This operation is idempotent - if a folder with the same UID or title exists, it will be skipped. Folders help organize dashboards by application, team, or environment.

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-grafana-config.yml`** — Verify that Grafana is properly configured. Checks that expected datasources exist and are healthy, required dashboards are present, and folders are created. Provides a comprehensive health check for Grafana observability setup.

## kibana

### config/

- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Enable anonymous access for Kibana in Tailscale mode. Patches the Kibana deployment to disable xpack security so users on the tailnet can access dashboards without logging in. Tailscale provides the authentication layer.
- **`05-wire-elastic.yml`** — Configure Kibana to connect to Elasticsearch. Kibana uses the ELASTICSEARCH_HOSTS environment variable (or kibana.yml config) to locate Elasticsearch. This playbook patches the Kibana deployment to set the correct internal K8s DNS URL for Elasticsearch, then waits for rollout and verifies connectivity.

## langfuse

### config/

- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Configure Langfuse for Tailscale Ingress mode. Sets NextAuth.js environment variables so Langfuse trusts the Tailscale proxy headers, listens on all interfaces, and keeps password auth as a fallback. NEXTAUTH_URL is pointed at the Tailscale IP on NodePort 30901.
- **`05-create-external-secret.yml`** — Create an ExternalSecret CRD in the ai-tools namespace that pulls Langfuse secrets from Vault via the ClusterSecretStore vault-backend. Creates a K8s Secret 'langfuse-secrets' with keys 'nextauth-secret' and 'salt' from separate Vault paths.
- **`06-wire-vault-secrets.yml`** — Replace hardcoded Langfuse secrets with an ExternalSecret CRD that pulls nextauth_secret and salt from Vault path apps/data/langfuse/. Requires a working ClusterSecretStore (vault-backend) from the external-secrets/04-wire-vault playbook. Creates the ExternalSecret in the ai-tools namespace.

### install/

- **`01-deploy.yml`** — Deploy Langfuse LLM observability platform to K3s cluster. Tracks token usage, traces, and provides analytics for AI workloads. Accessible via Tailscale on NodePort 30901.
  - Templates: `secrets.yaml.j2`, `postgres-statefulset.yaml.j2`, `postgres-service.yaml.j2`, `deployment.yaml.j2`, `service.yaml.j2`
- **`02-verify.yml`** — Verify Langfuse deployment is healthy

### operations/

- **`dataset-create.yml`** — Create an evaluation dataset in Langfuse. This operation is idempotent - if a dataset with the same name exists, it will be skipped. Datasets are used to store test cases for LLM evaluation. Langfuse uses Basic auth with public key as username and secret key as password.
- **`dataset-item-create.yml`** — Add an item to a Langfuse evaluation dataset. Dataset items contain input/output pairs used for testing LLM applications. This operation supports idempotency via custom item IDs. Langfuse uses Basic auth with public key as username and secret key as password.
- **`prompt-create.yml`** — Create or update a prompt in Langfuse. This operation creates a new prompt or a new version of an existing prompt. Langfuse uses Basic auth with public key as username and secret key as password.
- **`score-create.yml`** — Create a quality score for a trace or observation in Langfuse. Scores are used to evaluate LLM outputs (e.g., accuracy, relevance, helpfulness). Supports numeric, categorical, and boolean score types. This operation supports idempotency via custom score IDs. Langfuse uses Basic auth with public key as username and secret key as password.

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-langfuse-config.yml`** — Verify that Langfuse is properly configured. Checks that the API is accessible with valid credentials, expected prompts are created, and datasets exist. Provides a comprehensive health check for Langfuse LLM observability setup.

## loki

### config/

- **`05-wire-alertmanager.yml`** — Configure Loki's ruler component to send alerts to Alertmanager. Patches the loki-config ConfigMap to add the ruler section with alertmanager_url pointing to the Alertmanager K8s service, then restarts Loki to pick up the new config. Idempotent: checks if ruler alertmanager_url is already configured before patching.
- **`06-deploy-alloy.yml`** — Deploy Grafana Alloy DaemonSet for log collection into Loki. Loki is deployed but receives zero logs without a collector. Alloy runs on every node, collects from /var/log/pods/**/*.log using loki.source.kubernetes, and pushes to the Loki HTTP endpoint. Includes ServiceAccount with RBAC for pod/namespace discovery.
- **`07-enable-metrics.yml`** — Add Prometheus scrape annotations to the Loki statefulset. Loki natively exposes metrics on port 3100 at /metrics. This playbook adds pod-level annotations so Prometheus auto-discovers and scrapes the metrics endpoint via its kubernetes-pods scrape config.
- **`08-configure-alert-rules.yml`** — Push LogQL alert rules to the Loki Ruler via its HTTP API. The ruler must already be configured with alertmanager_url and enable_api: true (done by loki/config/05-wire-alertmanager.yml). Rules cover five log-based alerts: arr import failures, download client disconnects, vault audit errors, authentication failure spikes, and cert renewal errors. Uses the Loki Ruler API (POST /loki/api/v1/rules/{namespace}) to create or update rules. Idempotent: checks existing rules before pushing.
- **`09-enable-prometheus-remote-write.yml`** — Configure Loki's ruler to push Loki-derived metrics to Prometheus via remote_write. Also enables the remote write receiver on the Prometheus deployment. Patches both the Loki ConfigMap and the Prometheus deployment args, then restarts both services. Idempotent: checks existing config before patching.

- **`01-deploy.yml`** — Deploy Loki log aggregation system to K3s cluster. Provides centralized logging for all cluster workloads. Accessible via Tailscale on NodePort 30100.

- **`backup-create.yml`** — Create a Longhorn Backup for an existing volume. Backups are stored in the configured BackupTarget (S3, NFS, or Azure Blob). Each backup creates a new point-in-time copy. Requires a snapshot to exist or creates one automatically.
- **`setting-update.yml`** — Update a Longhorn Setting via CRD. Settings control Longhorn behavior such as backup target, replica count defaults, storage policies, etc. Common settings: backup-target, default-replica-count, storage-over-provisioning-percentage.
- **`snapshot-create.yml`** — Create a Longhorn Snapshot for an existing volume. Snapshots are local point-in-time copies stored within the Longhorn system. They are fast to create and can be used for quick rollbacks or as source for backups.
- **`volume-create.yml`** — Create a Longhorn Volume via CRD. This operation is idempotent - if a volume with the same name exists, it will be skipped. Supports all volume parameters: size, replicas, data locality, etc.

## neo4j

### config/

- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Disable Neo4j built-in authentication for Tailscale Ingress mode. Sets NEO4J_AUTH=none and NEO4J_dbms_security_auth__enabled=false on the StatefulSet so Neo4j Browser and Bolt do not require login. Tailscale provides the authentication layer.

### install/

- **`01-deploy.yml`** — Deploy Neo4j graph database to K3s cluster via J2 templates. Provides graph storage with APOC and vector search for GraphRAG. Accessible via NodePort 30474.
  - Templates: `secrets.yaml.j2`, `statefulset.yaml.j2`, `service.yaml.j2`, `configmap-schemas.yaml.j2`
- **`02-verify.yml`** — Verify Neo4j deployment is healthy

### operations/

- **`database-create.yml`** — Create a new database in Neo4j via the HTTP Transaction API. This operation is idempotent - uses CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS. Waits for the database to become online before completing. Note: Multi-database requires Neo4j Enterprise.
- **`index-create.yml`** — Create an index in Neo4j via the HTTP Transaction API. Supports multiple index types: range (default), text, fulltext, and composite. This operation is idempotent - uses IF NOT EXISTS clause. Waits for the index to become ONLINE.
- **`role-create.yml`** — Create a new role in Neo4j via the HTTP Transaction API. This operation is idempotent - uses CREATE ROLE IF NOT EXISTS. Optionally grants privileges and assigns the role to users. Note: Custom roles require Neo4j Enterprise.
- **`user-create.yml`** — Create a new user in Neo4j via the HTTP Transaction API. This operation is idempotent - if the user already exists, it will be skipped. Uses Cypher's CREATE USER command executed against the system database.

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-neo4j-config.yml`** — Verify that Neo4j is properly configured. Checks cluster health, database status, user existence, role configuration, index states, and constraint validity. Provides a comprehensive health report for Neo4j graph database setup.

## prometheus

### config/

- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Configure Prometheus for Tailscale Ingress mode. Sets --web.external-url so Prometheus generates correct self-referencing links when accessed via the Tailscale IP. Verifies --web.enable-lifecycle is present for remote config reload capability. Prometheus has no built-in authentication — Tailscale provides the network-level access control.
- **`05-wire-alertmanager.yml`** — Configure Prometheus to send alerts to Alertmanager. Prometheus uses a YAML config file (not an API) for alertmanager_config. This playbook patches the Prometheus ConfigMap to add the alerting.alertmanagers section pointing to the Alertmanager K8s service, then triggers a config reload via the /-/reload endpoint.
- **`06-enable-rule-files.yml`** — Add rule_files section to the Prometheus ConfigMap and mount a rules ConfigMap. Creates an empty prometheus-rules ConfigMap as a placeholder for alert rules, patches prometheus.yml to include rule_files pointing at /etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml, and mounts the rules ConfigMap into the Prometheus deployment. Triggers a config reload via /-/reload.
- **`07-configure-alert-rules.yml`** — Create or update the prometheus-rules ConfigMap in the observability namespace containing all Prometheus alert rules. Rules are split into two groups: infrastructure (cert-manager, vault, argocd, longhorn, external-secrets, traefik, authentik) and media-stack (sonarr, radarr, prowlarr, sabnzbd, qbittorrent, jellyfin, plex). The prerequisite playbook (06-enable-rule-files.yml) sets up the rule_files path and volume mount -- this playbook only manages the ConfigMap content. Prometheus watches ConfigMaps if configured with rule_files, so no restart is needed. Idempotent: skips apply if content hash unchanged.

### install/

## teleport

### config/

- **`01-configure-auth.yml`** — Configure Teleport authentication and create initial admin user
- **`04-configure-api.yml`** — Configure Teleport for Tailscale Ingress mode. Sets the public address to the Tailscale hostname so Teleport issues correct redirect URLs and trusts the proxy path. Also ensures TELEPORT_AUTH_TYPE=local so the built-in auth system remains active — Teleport is an access platform and cannot have auth disabled. This playbook makes Teleport ACCESSIBLE via the Tailscale network, not auth-bypassed.
- **`05-enable-metrics.yml`** — Enable Prometheus metrics scraping for Teleport. Patches the teleport-config ConfigMap to add diag_addr: "0.0.0.0:3434" which enables the diagnostics listener (health + metrics). Then adds pod-level Prometheus scrape annotations on port 3434 so Prometheus auto-discovers and scrapes the /metrics endpoint. Requires a StatefulSet restart for the ConfigMap change to take effect.
- **`06-wire-authentik-oidc.yml`** — Configure Teleport OIDC SSO connector backed by Authentik. Creates an OIDC connector resource via tctl that maps the Authentik admins group to the Teleport admin role. Uses kubectl exec to run tctl inside the Teleport pod.

### install/

- **`01-apply-kustomize.yml`** — Apply Teleport Kustomize manifests to K3s cluster
  - Templates: `namespace.yaml.j2`, `serviceaccount.yaml.j2`, `configmap.yaml.j2`, `statefulset.yaml.j2`, `service.yaml.j2`
- **`02-verify.yml`** — Verify Teleport is healthy and accessible

### operations/

- **`app-create.yml`** — Register an application with Teleport for secure access. This enables zero-trust application access with authentication, authorization, and audit logging. Applications can be internal web apps, APIs, or cloud consoles. Idempotent - skips if app already exists.
- **`oidc-connector-create.yml`** — Create an OIDC SSO connector in Teleport. This enables users to authenticate via external identity providers like Authentik, Okta, or Google Workspace. Claims are mapped to Teleport roles for authorization. Idempotent - skips if exists.
- **`role-create.yml`** — Create an RBAC role in Teleport. Roles define what resources users can access and what actions they can perform. This operation is idempotent - if the role exists, it will be skipped. Supports SSH, Kubernetes, database, and app access.
- **`user-create.yml`** — Create a local user in Teleport. Users are assigned roles that define their access permissions. This operation is idempotent - if the user exists, it will be skipped. For SSO users, use OIDC/SAML connector instead.

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-teleport-config.yml`** — Comprehensive verification of Teleport cluster configuration. Validates cluster health, auth connectors (OIDC/SAML/GitHub), RBAC roles, users with role assignments, registered applications, and connected nodes. Provides a detailed health report with optional fail_on_unhealthy behavior.

### config/

- **`00-init-unseal.yml`** — Initialize and unseal Vault, write root token and unseal key to BWS inventory
- **`01-sync-from-bws.yml`** — Sync secrets from Bitwarden Secrets Manager (BWS) to HashiCorp Vault KV store

Sets VAULT_UI, VAULT_API_ADDR, and VAULT_CLUSTER_ADDR environment variables on the Vault StatefulSet so the UI and API work correctly behind a Tailscale proxy. Vault still requires token-based login (auth cannot be disabled for a secrets engine). This playbook ensures the UI is ACCESSIBLE, not auth-bypassed.
- **`05-enable-telemetry.yml`** — Enable Vault Prometheus telemetry. Creates a ConfigMap with a Vault telemetry config overlay that sets prometheus_retention_time and unauthenticated_metrics_access on the listener. Patches the Vault StatefulSet to mount the overlay and sets VAULT_CONFIG_DIR to load it. After restart, /v1/sys/metrics is accessible without a token.
- **`06-enable-audit.yml`** — Enable Vault file audit device writing to stdout. Audit logs written to stdout are collected automatically by Alloy (DaemonSet) from /var/log/pods, so no persistent volume is required. Uses the Vault HTTP API with the root token to enable the audit device. Idempotent: checks if an audit device is already enabled before creating one.

### install/

- **`01-deploy-server.yml`** — Deploy HashiCorp Vault server to K3s cluster (Phase 4 handles init/unseal)
  - Templates: `serviceaccount.yaml.j2`, `config.yaml.j2`, `service.yaml.j2`, `statefulset.yaml.j2`
- **`02-verify.yml`** — Verify Vault deployment is healthy

### operations/

- **`vault-auth-kubernetes-enable.yml`** — Enable and configure Kubernetes authentication method in Vault. This operation is idempotent - if the kubernetes auth method is already enabled, only the configuration will be updated. Automatically retrieves K8s CA cert and service account JWT for configuration.
- **`vault-policy-create.yml`** — Create or update an ACL policy in Vault. Policies define what paths a token can access and what operations it can perform. This operation is idempotent - if the policy exists, it will be updated with the new rules.
- **`vault-secrets-kv-create.yml`** — Create a KV (Key-Value) secrets engine in Vault. Supports both KV v1 and KV v2. This operation is idempotent - if the secrets engine already exists at the specified path, it will be skipped. Default is KV v2 for versioned secrets.
- **`vault-sys-init.yml`** — Initialize Vault cluster. This operation is idempotent - if Vault is already initialized, it will be skipped. Stores root token and unseal keys in BWS _state for secure retrieval by subsequent operations.
- **`vault-sys-unseal.yml`** — Unseal Vault using unseal keys stored in BWS _state. This operation is idempotent - if Vault is already unsealed, it will be skipped. Automatically reads unseal keys from BWS and applies them until threshold is met.

### render/

- **`00-render-manifests.yml`** — Render Vault Kubernetes manifests from J2 templates using BWS inventory variables
  - Templates: `statefulset.yaml.j2`, `service.yaml.j2`, `config.yaml.j2`

### uninstall/

- **`01-remove.yml`** — Manifest: 01-remove.yml

### verify/

- **`01-verify-vault-init.yml`** — Comprehensive verification of Vault operational status. Validates that Vault is initialized, unsealed, auth methods are configured, and secrets engines are enabled. Returns detailed status report for each check.
